content:
The image shows soybean leaves with a distinct white, powdery/silvery coating covering the upper surfaces of leaves throughout the plant. The leaves themselves appear dark green beneath the coating, with the white dusty material visibly present across multiple leaves at different canopy levels.

Key observations:
- White to gray powdery coating on upper leaf surfaces, coalescing to cover large portions of leaves
- Leaves remain attached and appear otherwise intact (no necrosis or lesions with margins)
- No angular lesions, pustules, or water-soaking visible
- The coating has a characteristic dusty/powdery texture

This matches Powdery Mildew very closely: "White, powdery coating on leaves that begins as small patches and coalesces to cover entire leaves." The silvery-white surface coating visible across multiple leaves is the hallmark feature.

Downy mildew was considered but ruled out — that disease shows tufts of fungal growth specifically on the underside, and typically presents with yellow spots on upper surfaces first.
